items.title: Surface oracle feedback themes as 'What people want to know' discovery chips
items.why: api/oracle-feedback-themes.json is built at deploy time from oracle-feedback:<clusterId> RUM events — but it's never shown to visitors. The oracle page gets answers but has no 'warm start' signal showing what the community has been exploring. Surfacing the top-5 cluster chips above the oracle search box turns anonymous collective curiosity into a discovery mechanism: a first-time visitor sees 'Strategy · Membership · Monetization · Early Access · Leagues' and can orient instantly. This closes the feedback loop that was opened in S207 and has been collecting data ever since.
items.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js: at mount(), fetch api/oracle-feedback-themes.json, render top-5 ranked themes as clickable topic chips in a 'What our community is exploring' cluster above the starter prompts. On click: pre-fill oracle search with the theme label. Use existing starter-chip CSS classes (style-contract compliant). Add oracle:topic_chip_click to Worker RUM_UX_EVENTS.

L1.recipe: Read oracle-feedback-themes.json at IGNIS mount, render top 3 theme names as plain starter chips prefilling the search box

L2.recipe: L1 + labeled 'What the Vault is exploring:' section + click→search pre-fill + oracle:topic_chip_click RUM + graceful empty-state when <3 themes

L3.recipe: L2 + per-theme trending arrow (up/down vs prior session via build-oracle-feedback-themes.mjs) + theme ranking by recency weight

items.title: Topic-aware IGNIS re-entry: 'New content about [your topic] since your last visit'
items.why: The S210 returning-visitor signal strip surfaces any new changelog entry since vs_last_visit_ts — but it's blind to what the visitor actually cared about. A visitor who asked 'how does football GM monetize' three weeks ago gets the same generic 'New dispatch posted' chip as anyone else. Cross-referencing vs_ignis_history (their query topics) with changelog-narrative.json (new entries) makes the re-entry surface hyper-relevant: 'New intel matching your question about monetization — search it now →'. Nobody does this in the category.
items.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js renderResumeChip(): read vs_ignis_history (last 5 queries). Fetch api/changelog-narrative.json. Cross-reference changelog entry titles against query keywords (simple split + includes check). If a match exists and entry is newer than vs_last_visit_ts: show 'New intel about [keyword]' chip with vs_ignis_topic_chip:shown RUM. Reuse .vs-ignis-resume class; no new CSS.

L1.recipe: Check if any changelog entry is newer than vs_last_visit_ts; if so, add 'New content since your last visit' chip to existing resume chip

L2.recipe: Full topic cross-reference: vs_ignis_history keywords × changelog entry titles; render 'New intel about [keyword]' if matched; fallback to generic; RUM

L3.recipe: L2 + query ignis-query-index for documents newer than vs_last_visit_ts matching history keywords — surface as 'X new answers about [topic]'

items.title: IGNIS prefix cache: deploy-hash key clears stale answers on redeployment
items.why: The IGNIS prefix cache (vs_ignis_prefix_cache, 24h TTL) has no deploy-version key. When a deployment changes api/ignis-query-index.json, returning visitors see 'Continuing from your earlier search — [stale excerpt]' for up to 24h. api/build-sha.json exists from S210 — a one-check fix: if stored SHA !== current SHA, clear the prefix cache. Small correctness improvement with zero performance cost, meaningful trust improvement for the 'Continuing from earlier' pattern.
items.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js getPrefixCache(): fetch api/build-sha.json once per session (module-scope promise). Compare stored vs_ignis_deploy_sha vs current sha. If different: localStorage.removeItem(PREFIX_CACHE_KEY); update vs_ignis_deploy_sha. One async check protecting the full 24h cache window.

L1.recipe: Fetch api/build-sha.json at IGNIS init; compare vs vs_ignis_deploy_sha; clear prefix cache on mismatch; update sha key

L2.recipe: L1 + include sha in PREFIX_CACHE_KEY itself so each deploy gets a fresh namespace; old keys expire via storage quota

L3.recipe: L2 + soft-stale window: keep entries <2h old from prior deployment as warm fallback while fresh index loads

items.verifyNote: Confirmed: PREFIX_CACHE_KEY = 'vs_ignis_prefix_cache' with no sha component. api/build-sha.json exists (S210). No deploy-hash check found in cache read/write path.

items.title: CSP violation reporting pipeline: report-uri → Worker RUM → doctor probe
items.why: The CSP headers block unsafe scripts and untrusted origins — but violations are completely silent. No report-uri endpoint exists. The Worker handles /v/rum RUM beacons already. Adding /v/csp-report (standard CSP violation JSON POST) takes ~20 Worker lines and creates a real-time security signal: CSP violations (injected ads, browser extension conflicts, new untrusted assets) surface in the doctor table instead of arriving via user complaint. CANON-051 Web Hardening baseline requires CSP — monitoring it is the natural second step.
items.recipe: Worker: add /v/csp-report route that parses the JSON POST body, increments KV counter csp:violations:date, stores top-3 blocked-uri + violated-directive. Add report-uri https://vaultsparkstudios.com/v/csp-report to the CSP header in _headers. Build scripts/check-csp-violations.mjs reading api/csp-violations.json for doctor probe.

L1.recipe: Worker: /v/csp-report handler that increments a KV counter + returns 204. Add report-uri to _headers CSP.

L2.recipe: L1 + structured violation log (blocked-uri, violated-directive, top-5/day) + build-csp-violations.mjs → api/csp-violations.json + doctor probe warns on >10/day

L3.recipe: L2 + report-to header (Reporting API) + ci-health-monitor integration (auto-issue on spike >100/day)

items.verifyNote: Confirmed: Worker handles /v/rum but no /v/csp-report. _headers CSP has no report-uri. CANON-051 compliance gap — CSP is set but unmonitored.

items.title: IGNIS session-aware query expansion: boost results matching prior session queries
items.why: The oracle is a static document retrieval engine that scores documents against the current query with no session context. A visitor who asked 'football gm draft strategy' and then asks 'how do I win' gets generic results, not football-strategy-amplified results. sessionStorage already holds the last 5 queries (vs_ignis_history). A lightweight query-expansion pass: extract top-N keywords from session history, apply a contextBoost multiplier (+0.15) in the scoring loop when a document's title/tags match a history keyword. All client-side, zero new API calls.
items.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js query(): read sessionStorage vs_ignis_history, extract top-3 keywords (split + stop-word filter). In the document scoring loop: add +0.15 contextBoost when document title/tags include a history keyword. Only apply when ≥2 prior queries (prevents single-query over-specialization). Cap at 2× raw score. Add oracle:context_boost RUM event.

L1.recipe: Extract keywords from vs_ignis_history; console.log boost candidates (no visible change — A/B verification)

L2.recipe: Full context boost in scoring: +0.15 per session-keyword match, capped 2×; only ≥2 prior queries; oracle:context_boost RUM

L3.recipe: L2 + session decay (recent queries weighted more) + explicit 'based on your interest in X' label on boosted results

items.verifyNote: Confirmed: vs_ignis_history in sessionStorage (S211). Oracle scoring is stateless per-query. No context expansion found in ignis-answer-engine.js. Clean gap.

items.title: Lighthouse CI blocking gate: check-lighthouse-trend --check in workflow post-run
items.why: check-lighthouse-trend.mjs seeds + tracks per-page LH scores (S225) and RAW_METRICS (S226). But it only runs locally — the CI Lighthouse workflow still uses a raw threshold with no session-over-session regression detection. Adding --check --session N as a post-run step makes ≥0.05 regression from best-session blocking in CI. This closes the multi-session blind spot where Lighthouse quietly declined from 0.88 to 0.76 without a gate catching it (the S209-S225 incident).
items.recipe: In .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml: after all Lighthouse runs complete, add a step running 'node scripts/check-lighthouse-trend.mjs --check'. The --check flag already exits 1 on regression (S225). Commit the lighthouse-trend.json baseline update in the same CI step.

L2.recipe: L1 + auto-update .cache/lighthouse-trend.json baseline via CI artifact upload + cache-restore

L3.recipe: L2 + --threshold flag per workflow + failure annotation naming the specific page that regressed

items.why: The push dispatch sends the same title/body to all subscribers. The Worker already stores lastGame per subscriber in KV (S213). GAME_COPY_VARIANTS simply doesn't exist yet. 'Call of Doodie just dropped a new challenge' converts at dramatically higher rates than 'New from VaultSpark Studios' for a subscriber who identified as a CoD player. This turns the push system from a broadcast into a relevance engine — and the data is already there.

When iterating subscribers: read sub.lastGame from KV data; select matching variant. Pass game-specific title+body to push dispatch. Add push:personalized RUM in sw.js.

items.title: check-sitemap-coverage.mjs: gate sitemap completeness against page generators
items.why: sitemap.xml is manually maintained. The leaderboard sub-pages TASK_BOARD item was stale — all 7 entries already exist (phantom-detected this session). But the class is real: future page generators can ship without adding sitemap entries. A gate that scans known page generators (build-leaderboard-subpages.mjs PAGES, propagate-nav.mjs) and verifies each generated URL in sitemap.xml makes the gap detectable on the very next build. Converts a phantom carry into a second-order gate.
items.recipe: Build scripts/check-sitemap-coverage.mjs: reads sitemap.xml into a Set of <loc> URLs. Imports PAGES from build-leaderboard-subpages.mjs. Globs games/*/index.html and projects/*/index.html. For each page URL not in sitemap Set: warn. Self-test 5 cases: all present, one missing, empty pages, missing sitemap, wrong export. Wire into check-proof-surface.mjs.

L2.recipe: Full generator-aware check: import PAGES from generators, compare against sitemap Set, warn on gaps, self-test 5/5, wire into check-proof-surface

L3.recipe: L2 + --fix mode: auto-add missing entries to sitemap.xml + check lastmod dates are current
